task: D-FALCO-NOISE: after the Falco 0.45.1 rollout the bundled rule 'Contact K8S API Server From Container' produced all but two of the events in live Loki, all from platform components that are expected to call the API. Add a narrow, appended exception for the 8 exact (k8s.ns.name, container.image.repository) pairs through the chart's customRules, pin it in R291 (A11) and record it in falco.yaml, the CHANGELOGs and the lessons-log. No cluster access and no push: the live counts are supplied by the coordinator, and the behaviour of the exception was checked with the real falco:0.45.1 image in a local Docker lab only.

events.summary: Add ONE appended exception to the bundled rule 'Contact K8S API Server From Container' through the chart's customRules (ConfigMap falco-rules on /etc/falco/rules.d) for the 8 exact (k8s.ns.name, container.image.repository) pairs from the decision D-FALCO-NOISE, with override.exceptions: append; record the decision in falco.yaml; pin it in R291 as assertion A11 with mutations; CHANGELOG EN/KO, a lessons-log row and this trace. Deliberately left alone: the bundled macro user_known_contact_k8s_api_server_activities, falco.priority and loki.minimumpriority (no raised floor), the falco and falcosidekick versions and resources, the portal, and every other rule. No cluster access, no push, no namespace-wide or image-wide wildcard.

events.summary: Supplied, not observed here: DaemonSet 6/6, 0 restarts, 41-68Mi; 47,180 events in 20 h, 47,178 of them the rule 'Contact K8S API Server From Container' (Notice); per (k8s.ns.name, container.image.repository): storage docker.io/otwld/velero-ui 43013, devtools ghcr.io/dasomel/narwhal-portal 2084, iam quay.io/keycloak/keycloak-operator 1807, platform-system reg.kyverno.io/kyverno/kyverno 360, devtools ghcr.io/headlamp-k8s/headlamp 8, devtools docker.io/kubernetesui/dashboard-auth 1, devtools docker.io/kubernetesui/dashboard-web 1, platform-system ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/cloudnative-pg 1. Cross-checked against the real image: the rule text, its condition, the macro user_known_contact_k8s_api_server_activities = (never_true) and required_engine_version 0.57.0 are as described (see e3). Not verifiable here: every live count. Arithmetic on the supplied numbers: the 8 pair counts sum to 47,275 and the first four alone to 47,264, which is above both the 47,180 total and the 47,178 rule total, so the totals and the pair counts come from different queries; the decision record says so.

The mechanism was reproduced in a local Docker lab on the real docker.io/falcosecurity/falco:0.45.1 (Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit, modern_ebpf, the falco.yaml the chart renders from the repo values with only http_output off and the docker engine instead of cri). The bundled rule has no exceptions key and its only hook is the never_true macro, so any container that connects to the API-server name fires it: with no rules.d file, 10 lab clients that each connect once to the address kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local resolves to (an --add-host entry in the Falco container) produce 10 Notice events, one each, with k8s.ns.name taken from the io.kubernetes.pod.namespace label (null without it). That is the event shape the supplied live data describes; the live volume itself was not reproduced.

events.summary: falco.yaml gains a top-level customRules value with one file, narwhal-api-noise.yaml: a rule item named exactly 'Contact K8S API Server From Container' with override: {exceptions: append} and one exception, narwhal_platform_api_clients, fields [k8s.ns.name, container.image.repository], comps [=, =], and the 8 reviewed pairs. The chart renders it as ConfigMap falco-rules mounted on /etc/falco/rules.d, which falco.rules_files loads after falco_rules.yaml; checksum/rules makes the DaemonSet roll. The header records D-FALCO-NOISE: the supplied data, the cost (those 8 workloads' API connections are no longer flagged; the kube-apiserver audit policy still records their writes and their reads of secrets, configmaps, serviceaccounts and RBAC objects, other get/list/watch are not audited), what was deliberately not done and the escape hatch. falco.priority, loki.minimumpriority, the bundled macro, versions and resources are unchanged.

R291 gets assertion A11 for the exception: exactly one custom item, the bundled rule name exactly, override exactly {exceptions: append} (a replace is a valid file for Falco 0.45.1 but would drop exceptions appended elsewhere), exactly the keys name/fields/comps/values, fields and comps exactly as specified, every value a [namespace, repository] pair of non-empty strings with a Kubernetes namespace name, a registry-qualified repository and no glob character, no duplicate, the set equal to the 8 reviewed pairs; falco.priority stays notice, rules.d loads after the bundled rules, and the exception was validated against falco 0.45.1 only, so an image bump fails A11 until it is re-validated (a rules file Falco cannot load stops it). 19 new mutations, each caught by its own [A11] message; check-falco.py --mutation-verify now catches 69. A rule loader keeps a bare = a string, which PyYAML otherwise cannot construct.

CHANGELOG.md and CHANGELOG-ko.md get an Unreleased Fixed entry, gitops/README.md and README-ko.md one sentence in their Falco paragraph; docs/common/lessons-log.md gets a row (Korean, three columns) with the supplied live numbers and their provenance, the two shortcuts that were avoided, how a bad exception file fails, the validation results, the cost, and the post-deploy check; the R291 description in regression-check-kakao.sh names A11 and 69 mutations.
